topic: off-by-one error in a loop bound (<= vs <)
question: Quick reminder — what was the actual root cause?
butterfly_answer: Off-by-one in `process_batch` (`etl/pipeline.py:87`): `range(n+1)` iterated `n+1` times instead of `n`, so the last iteration processed an out-of-bounds index. Fixed by changing to `range(n)`.
lastN_answer: The prior context doesn't state what the root cause was — the conversation was entirely tangents. Never surfaced.
needle_fact: The root cause was that a PR titled 'fix: ensure last record processed' changed `for i in range(n)` to `for i in range(n + 1)` in process_batch at etl/pipeline.py:87, based on a misunderstanding of Python's half-open range semantics — `range(n)` already covers all valid indices 0..n-1 of a list of length n, so the change caused an IndexError on `records[n]`. The bug was missed by tests because test_process_batch used a MagicMock whose __getitem__ returned a valid value for any index.
